data.cultural_impact: The name 'Shawwan' holds a special place in Islamic culture, as it is a traditional Arabic name. It carries the essence of sunshine and brightness, which are considered positive symbols in various aspects of Islamic life. For instance, in Islamic art, bright colors and the image of the sun are often used to represent happiness, generosity, and prosperity. Similarly, this name could be given to a newborn on a sunny day to wish for a bright future filled with blessings, happiness and success.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Shawwan' is significant because it makes reference to one of the most powerful and life-giving symbols in creation - the sun. In the Islamic faith, the sun is seen as a reminder of Allah's power and mercy. The hadith relates that the Prophet Muhammad (PEAS) said, "Allah is beautiful and loves beauty," and that the sun and the moon were made beautiful for the sake of the believers. Thus, the name 'Shawwan' carries the spiritual meaning of being a reminder of the Creator's majesty and the divine gift of life. It can serve as an inspiration for the person named Shawwan to strive for the betterment of his soul by seeking knowledge, expressing gratitude to Allah for the blessings of life, and adhering to Islamic values.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name of a Caliph by the name of Shawwan al-Mustansir, who ruled the Abbasid Caliphate from 1332 to 1336 CE. His reign was marked by rebellions and political instability.

The prophet Muhammad is said to have sent an expedition to Shawwan, a region in southern Arabia, during his final pilgrimage in 632 CE. The purpose of the expedition was to secure the trade routes and protect Muslim caravans from raiders.
historical_references.context: Prophet Muhammad, trade protection, southern Arabia

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shawwan' is of Arabic origin and translates to 'the third' in English. In the Islamic calendar, Shawwan is the 12th month of the lunar year, which corresponds to late May or early June in the Gregorian calendar. Shawwan is a significant month in Middle Eastern culture, as it marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan. During this time, many people celebrate Eid Al-Fitr, a festive holiday marking the end of the Islamic holy month of Ramadan. On Instagram, Shawwan is seen as a popular hashtag for posts related to Eid Al-Fitr celebrations, foods, and traditional clothing. On YouTube, Shawwan is a popular search term for videos of Eid Al-Fitr prayers and holiday traditions, as well as recipes for traditional Shawwan dishes like shawarma and man'oushe. On Pinterest, Shawwan is a popular board theme for collecting and sharing ideas for Eid Al-Fitr decorations, clothing, and recipes.
